<![CDATA[News]]> /news/post en Copyright 2015 2015-04-30T22:18:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Announces Latest Slate Of Appointments]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-latest-slate-of-appointments-10-30 https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-latest-slate-of-appointments-10-30#When:21:30:00Z State Securities Board – Governor Abbott appointed Glenn MacTaggart and Paula Ann Miller to the State Securities Board for terms set to expire on January 20, 2031. Additionally, the Governor named MacTaggart Chair of the Board. The Board registers securities offered and sold in Texas and oversees the firms and individuals selling securities or providing investment advice to Texans.

Texas Woman’s University Board Of Regents – Governor Abbott appointed Rienke Radler to the Texas Woman’s University Board of Regents for a term set to expire on February 1, 2029. 

]]> 2026-10-30T21:30:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Announces Additional Federal Disaster Assistance Following July Storms And Flooding]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-additional-federal-disaster-assistance-following-july-storms-and-flooding https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-additional-federal-disaster-assistance-following-july-storms-and-flooding#When:20:20:00Z Governor Greg Abbott today announced that the federal government has approved Texas' appeal for Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Individual Assistance program funding following severe storms and flooding that impacted communities across the state in July.

The approval comes after an announcement from President Donald J. Trump this week, noting that the Trump Administration would make additional FEMA relief available following the July storms. This follows an appeal submitted by the State of Texas through the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM).

“President Trump has approved Texas’ appeal for FEMA Individual Assistance after the July storms and flooding,” said Governor Abbott. "This brings essential financial assistance and services to eligible Texans in the 20 approved counties. I thank President Trump for his leadership and for this additional support for Texas families.”

The following 20 counties are now approved for FEMA Individual Assistance: Bandera, Bexar, Comal, Crockett, Dimmit, Frio, Gillespie, Kendall, Kerr, Kimble, Kinney, La Salle, Maverick, Medina, Real, Schleicher, Sutton, Uvalde, Val Verde, and Zavala. Texans can apply for FEMA disaster assistance online at disasterassistance.gov or by calling 800-621-3362.

FEMA's Individual Assistance program provides eligible Texans with financial assistance and services for disaster-related expenses, including temporary housing, emergency home repairs, uninsured and underinsured personal property losses, disaster legal services, disaster unemployment assistance, and medical, dental, and funeral expenses caused by the disaster.

Additionally, an appeal to FEMA for Hazard Mitigation grant program funding remains pending.

Governor Abbott continues to take action to provide all available resources to support communities impacted by the July severe storms and flooding, including:

  • Obtaining a suspension on federal tax deadlines for affected Texans and businesses
  • Calling for suspension of federal tax deadlines for impacted Texans and businesses
  • Acquiring federal disaster assistance for four additional counties that sustained storm impacts
  • Requesting federal disaster assistance for additional affected counties
  • Securing approval of a Major Disaster Declaration following storm impacts
  • Communicating the further extension of SNAP replacement benefits for Texans affected by flooding
  • Amending the state’s disaster declaration to include additional impacted counties and providing an update in Cotulla on the state’s emergency response in affected areas
  • Surveying flood-damaged communities and communicating updates on the state’s response posture.
  • Announcing the extension of SNAP replacement benefits for Texans affected by flooding
  • Providing an update in Uvalde on the state’s flood response and requesting federal disaster assistance
  • Sharing additional updates on Texas’ flood response operations
  • Updating Texans on the statewide flood response
  • Issuing a state disaster declaration, increasing the readiness level of the Texas State Emergency Operations (SOC) to 24-hour operations at Level II (Escalated Response) and activating additional state emergency response resources as heavy rainfall and flash flooding threats continued
  • Deploying state emergency response resources ahead of the severe weather and flash flooding threat
]]> 2026-10-30T20:20:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Declares El Paso County Flooding Disaster In October 2026]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-declares-el-paso-county-flooding-disaster-in-october-2026 https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-declares-el-paso-county-flooding-disaster-in-october-2026#When:21:16:00Z TO ALL TO WHOM THESE PRESENTS SHALL COME:

WHEREAS, I, GREG ABBOTT, Governor of the State of Texas, do hereby certify that the severe storm event that began on October 23, 2026, and that included heavy rainfall and flash flooding, poses a threat of imminent disaster, including widespread and severe property damage, injury, or loss of life in El Paso County;

NOW, THEREFORE, in accordance with the authority vested in me by Section 418.014 of the Texas Government Code, I do hereby declare a state of disaster in El Paso County.

Pursuant to Section 418.017 of the Texas Government Code, I authorize the use of all available resources of state government and of political subdivisions that are reasonably necessary to cope with this disaster.

Pursuant to Section 418.016 of the Texas Government Code, any regulatory statute prescribing the procedures for conduct of state business or any order or rule of a state agency that would in any way prevent, hinder, or delay necessary action in coping with this disaster shall be suspended upon written approval of the Office of the Governor.  However, to the extent that the enforcement of any state statute or administrative rule regarding contracting or procurement would impede any state agency’s emergency response that is necessary to protect life or property threatened by this declared disaster, I hereby authorize the suspension of such statutes and rules for the duration of this declared disaster.

In accordance with the statutory requirements, copies of this proclamation shall be filed with the applicable authorities.

IN TESTIMONY WHEREOF, I have hereunto signed my name and have officially caused the Seal of State to be affixed at my office in the City of Austin, Texas, this the 29th day of October, 2026.

 

GREG ABBOTT

Governor

 

ATTESTED BY:

ROBERT HOWDEN

Secretary of State

 

View the Governor's proclamation. 

]]> 2026-10-29T21:16:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Issues State Disaster Declaration For El Paso County Following Flooding Impacts]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-issues-state-disaster-declaration-for-el-paso-county-following-flooding-impacts https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-issues-state-disaster-declaration-for-el-paso-county-following-flooding-impacts#When:21:13:00Z Governor Greg Abbott today announced that he has issued a state disaster declaration for El Paso County following heavy rainfall and flooding that has impacted communities in the Far West Texas region.

“I issued a state disaster declaration for El Paso County to ensure the full resources of the State of Texas are available to support local response and recovery after heavy rainfall and flooding,” said Governor Abbott. “Texans affected by this storm should report damage through the iSTAT survey once it is safe so officials can assess needs and eligibility for federal assistance. Texans must never drive through flooded roads and should follow guidance from local officials.”

State emergency response resources deployed by the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) at the Governor’s direction remain engaged in support of local response and recovery efforts.

When it is safe to do so, the Governor also urged Texans affected by recent rain and flooding to report damage online using TDEM’s Individual State of Texas Assessment Tool (iSTAT) damage survey. The self-reporting damage survey is available online at damage.tdem.texas.gov. The information provided by Texans in the iSTAT survey aids emergency management officials in gaining an understanding of damage that has occurred, helps officials determine whether federal requirements for various forms of disaster assistance have been met, and identifies any immediate resource needs.

As additional rainfall and flooding threats continue, hazardous conditions remain an ongoing concern. Texans are reminded to monitor local weather forecasts, follow guidance from emergency management officials, and never drive through flooded roadways. Texans can find flood safety information at TexasReady.gov, check road conditions at DriveTexas.org, access flood information at TexasFlood.org, and locate all-hazards preparedness tips at tdem.texas.gov/prepare.

]]> 2026-10-29T21:13:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Announces $87 Million In Rural Healthcare Grants]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-87-million-in-rural-healthcare-grants https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-87-million-in-rural-healthcare-grants#When:19:05:00Z Governor Greg Abbott today announced that the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC) plans to award $87 million in Rural Texas Strong grants to 129 rural healthcare providers throughout the state.

“Rural Texas communities deserve access to top-notch, reliable care,” said Governor Abbott. “This more than $87 million investment will help to recruit and retain the next generation of healthcare professionals, replace aging medical equipment, and strengthen facilities across Texas communities to improve patient outcomes.”

“The Trump Administration’s Rural Health Transformation Program is equipping states with the resources they need to strengthen rural health care and help families get better care closer to home,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “These investments will help Texas improve health outcomes, strengthen its rural health workforce, and give providers the tools and resources they need to deliver high-quality care.”

“These awards will build on the work medical teams do every day to care for rural Texans,” said HHS Executive Commissioner Stephanie Muth. “With this support, rural communities can respond to changing needs and sustain the healthcare services Texans rely on.”

Funding announced today will advance the following Rural Texas Strong initiatives:

  • The “Make Rural Texans Healthy Again” initiative helps rural hospital districts improve health outcomes and chronic disease conditions such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic respiratory disease, or obesity.
  • The “Next Generation of the Small Town Doctor and Team” initiative supports rural communities in recruiting, training and retaining physicians, emergency medical professionals, and other health care workers.
  • The “Infrastructure and Capital Investments for Rural Texas” initiative supports rural healthcare providers by replacing aging medical equipment and improving existing facilities.

The awards are part of a historic investment of an estimated $1.4 billion in federal funding over five years to improve rural healthcare throughout the state.

The $87,248,124.49 is a portion of the $281,319,360.67 first‑year award HHSC received from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Rural Health Transformation Program.

Rural Texas Strong, the CMS-approved state plan, is 100% federally funded through the Rural Health Transformation Program and features six initiatives to provide funding for rural communities to improve access to healthcare. Federal funding is contingent upon meeting all applicable program requirements.

HHSC will continue to announce its intent to award funding on a weekly basis as applications are reviewed across the Rural Texas Strong initiatives. Funding will be available after contracts are finalized. A list of all the recipients is available here.

For more information, visit the HHSC Rural Health Transformation webpage. Public notices and procurement opportunities for Rural Texas Strong will be announced through GovDelivery email notifications.

]]> 2026-10-29T19:05:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Announces Over $1.7 Million In Job Training Grants To Houston And Rio Grande Valley Areas]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-over-1.7-million-in-job-training-grants-to-houston-and-rio-grande-valley-areas https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-over-1.7-million-in-job-training-grants-to-houston-and-rio-grande-valley-areas#When:15:49:00Z Governor Greg Abbott today announced four Skills Development Fund (SDF) grant awards totaling $1,726,092 to Houston City College, Workforce Solutions Lower Rio Grande Valley, and local partners. These grants, administered by the Texas Workforce Commission (TWC), will help provide customized training for 689 new and current workers in high-demand occupations in manufacturing, technology, logistics, and more.

“Texas is the best state in the nation for job creation and economic opportunity,” said Governor Abbott. “These grants will equip 689 Texans with the skills they need for high-demand careers, help businesses find qualified workers, and ensure our state remains a leader in economic growth.”

“When we align local training directly with the needs of expanding industries, we strengthen the regional economy,” said TWC Chairman Joe Esparza. “These Skills Development Fund grants empower Houston City College and Workforce Solutions Lower Rio Grande Valley to provide the specialized, high-demand training that employers need to succeed right here in Texas.”

Yesterday, TWC Chairman Joe Esparza presented the awards to representatives from Houston City College, Tesla Inc., Watchfire Signs LLC, Texas Tissue Converting LLC, Karsten Management LLC, and other local partners during a ceremony held at Houston City College.

The three SDF grants include:

  • $782,998 to train 261 workers at Tesla Inc. as maintenance technicians, process technicians, welders, and more.
  • $690,044 to train 300 workers at Texas Tissue LLC and Karsten Management LLC as maintenance technicians, production line operators, design specialists, and frontline supervisors.
  • $83,963 to train 41 workers at Watchfire Signs LLC as operations specialists, industrial maintenance technicians, production supervisors, and more.

In addition, TWC Commissioner Representing Labor Alberto Treviño III presented a $169,087 award yesterday during a ceremony held at Rio Bank – McColl Center in McAllen. Through this grant, Workforce Solutions Lower Rio Grande Valley will provide customized training for 87 new and current workers at Denso Ten America Limited, Alps Logistics (USA) Inc., Index Fresh Inc., and Emerson Electric Co. for high-demand occupations in manufacturing, transportation, and more.

SDF is the state's workforce training grant program to help businesses upskill their new or incumbent workforce. In partnership with the public community and technical colleges, workforce development boards, Texas A&M Engineering Experiment Station, and Texas A&M Engineering Extension Service, TWC collaborates to provide customized, innovative training to Texas businesses of all sizes.

The SDF grant program has provided training opportunities in partnership with more than 5,000 employers to upgrade or support the creation of over 446,000 jobs throughout Texas since the program's inception in 1996.

]]> 2026-10-29T15:49:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Renews Diesel Fuel Shortage Disaster Proclamation In October 2026]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-renews-diesel-fuel-shortage-disaster-proclamation-in-october-2026 https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-renews-diesel-fuel-shortage-disaster-proclamation-in-october-2026#When:22:02:00Z TO ALL TO WHOM THESE PRESENTS SHALL COME:

WHEREAS, I, Greg Abbott, Governor of Texas, issued a disaster proclamation on September 28, 2026, certifying under Section 418.014 of the Texas Government Code that the shortage of diesel fuel poses an imminent threat or occurrence of harm to the public health and safety in the State of Texas, and declared a state of disaster for all Texas counties; and

WHEREAS, the certified conditions continue to exist and pose an ongoing and imminent threat of disaster as set forth in the Proclamation of September 28, 2026;

NOW, THEREFORE, in accordance with the authority vested in me by Section 418.014 of the Texas Government Code, I do hereby renew the aforementioned proclamation and declare a state of disaster for all Texas counties.  All orders, directions, suspensions, and authorizations provided in the Proclamation of September 28, 2026, as renewed, are in full force and effect.

In accordance with the statutory requirements, copies of this proclamation shall be filed with the applicable authorities.

IN TESTIMONY WHEREOF, I have hereunto signed my name and have officially caused the Seal of State to be affixed at my office in the City of Austin, Texas, this the 28th day of October, 2026. 

 

GREG ABBOTT

Governor

 

ATTESTED BY:

ROBERT HOWDEN

Secretary of State

 

View the Governor's proclamation. 

]]> 2026-10-28T22:02:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Activates State Emergency Response Resources Ahead of Texas Flood Threat]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-activates-state-emergency-response-resources-ahead-of-texas-flood-threat https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-activates-state-emergency-response-resources-ahead-of-texas-flood-threat#When:19:19:00Z Governor Greg Abbott today directed the Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) to activate state emergency response resources ahead of heavy rainfall and potential flash flooding expected to impact portions of West and South-Central Texas beginning tomorrow.

“The State of Texas is prepared to respond to the threat of heavy rainfall and flash flooding,” said Governor Abbott. “I directed the Texas Division of Emergency Management to activate state emergency response resources to support local officials and safeguard Texans. Texans should monitor local forecasts, heed guidance from state and local officials, and avoid flooded roadways.”

According to the National Weather Service, multiple storm systems associated with the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Vance and gulf moisture are expected to bring widespread thunderstorms capable of producing heavy rainfall and flash flooding across portions of the state. The greatest concern for excessive rainfall is expected Thursday across portions of West and South-Central Texas, including the Permian Basin, Big Bend, South Plains, Big Country, Hill Country, and Texas Border regions over the next couple of days.

At the direction of Governor Abbott, the following state emergency response resources are available to support local severe weather and flood operations:

  • Texas A&M Engineering Extension Service (Texas A&M Task Force 1): Swiftwater Rescue Boat Squads and high profile vehicles to assist with flood rescues
  • Texas Division of Emergency Management: Regional personnel to support deployed emergency response resources across the state
  • Texas Department of Transportation: Personnel monitoring roadway and transportation conditions
  • Texas Parks and Wildlife Department: Game Wardens, rescue boat teams, and helicopters with hoist capability to assist with water rescues
  • Texas Department of Public Safety: Texas Highway Patrol Troopers, helicopters with hoist capability, and the Tactical Marine Unit
  • Texas Department of State Health Services (Texas Emergency Medical Task Force): Severe Weather Support Packages consisting of medics, ambulances, and all-terrain vehicles
  • Texas A&M AgriLife Extension Service: Disaster Assessment and Recovery Agents and County Extension Agents to support agricultural and livestock needs
  • Public Utility Commission of Texas: Power-outage monitoring and coordination with utility providers
  • Railroad Commission of Texas: Monitoring of the state's natural gas supply and communication with the oil and gas industry
  • Texas Commission on Environmental Quality: Air, water, and wastewater monitoring

Texans are encouraged to remain weather-aware, follow instructions from local officials, review family emergency plans, and prepare an emergency supply kit. Never attempt to drive or walk through floodwater. Remember: Turn Around, Don't Drown.

Texans can check road conditions at DriveTexas.org, find severe weather safety tips at TexasReady.gov, access flood information at TexasFlood.org, and visit tdem.texas.gov/prepare for all-hazards preparedness information.

]]> 2026-10-28T19:19:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Appoints Radler To Texas Woman’s University Board Of Regents]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-appoints-radler-to-texas-womans-university-board-of-regents https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-appoints-radler-to-texas-womans-university-board-of-regents#When:18:02:00Z Governor Abbott appointed Rienke Radler to the Texas Woman’s University Board of Regents for a term set to expire on February 1, 2029. 

Rienke Radler of Fort Worth is a community volunteer and philanthropist. Previously, she worked as a physiotherapist in South Africa and the United Kingdom. She is a former gubernatorial appointee on the Governor’s Commission for Women and is an administrative leader at Bible Study Fellowship International. Radler received a Bachelor of Science in Physiotherapy from the University of the Free State in South Africa.

]]> 2026-10-28T18:02:00+00:00 <![CDATA[Governor Abbott Announces Federal Disaster Tax Relief For Texans Impacted By July Storms]]> https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-federal-disaster-tax-relief-for-texans-impacted-by-july-storms https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-announces-federal-disaster-tax-relief-for-texans-impacted-by-july-storms#When:14:35:00Z Governor Greg Abbott today announced that the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) granted his request for federal disaster tax relief for individuals and businesses in 62 Texas counties impacted by July’s severe storms and flooding.

“Texans who took damage from the July storms and floods now have more time to file and pay federal taxes,” said Governor Abbott. “I thank Secretary Bessent and the IRS for this relief to help families and businesses rebuild.”

Governor Abbott issued a state disaster proclamation on July 14 covering 62 counties. On October 15, the Governor requested this tax relief for taxpayers in all 62 counties.

The IRS postponed certain federal tax filing and payment deadlines through February 1, 2027, for taxpayers who reside or have a business in the 62 counties.

The counties included are: Atascosa, Austin, Bandera, Bastrop, Bexar, Blanco, Brazoria, Brewster, Burnet, Caldwell, Colorado, Comal, Crockett, DeWitt, Dimmit, Edwards, Fayette, Fort Bend, Frio, Galveston, Gillespie, Goliad, Gonzales, Grimes, Guadalupe, Harris, Hays, Jackson, Karnes, Kendall, Kerr, Kimble, Kinney, La Salle, Lavaca, Lee, Live Oak, Llano, Mason, Matagorda, Maverick, McMullen, Medina, Menard, Mitchell, Pecos, Real, Schleicher, Sutton, Terrell, Travis, Uvalde, Val Verde, Victoria, Waller, Washington, Webb, Wharton, Williamson, Wilson, Zapata, and Zavala.
